{{Short description|Mathematical result in the theory of Sobolev spaces}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Aubin–Lions lemma''' (or '''theorem''') is the result in the theory of [[Sobolev space]]s of [[Banach space]]-valued functions, which provides a [[compact space|compactness]] criterion that is useful in the study of nonlinear evolutionary [[partial differential equation]]s. Typically, to prove the existence of solutions one first constructs approximate solutions (for example, by a [[Galerkin method]] or by [[Mollifiers|mollification]] of the equation), then uses the compactness lemma to show that there is a convergent subsequence of approximate solutions whose limit is a solution.

The result is named after the [[France|French]] [[mathematician]]s [[Jean-Pierre Aubin]] and [[Jacques-Louis Lions]]. In the original proof by Aubin,<ref>{{harvtxt|Aubin|1963}}</ref> the spaces ''X''<sub>0</sub> and ''X''<sub>1</sub> in the statement of the lemma were assumed to be [[reflexive space|reflexive]], but this assumption was removed by Simon,<ref>{{harvtxt|Simon|1986}}</ref> so the result is also referred to as the '''Aubin–Lions–Simon  lemma'''.<ref>{{harvtxt|Boyer|Fabrie|2013}}</ref>

==Statement of the lemma==

Let ''X''<sub>0</sub>, ''X'' and ''X''<sub>1</sub> be three Banach spaces with ''X''<sub>0</sub>&nbsp;⊆&nbsp;''X''&nbsp;⊆&nbsp;''X''<sub>1</sub>.  Suppose that ''X''<sub>0</sub> is [[compactly embedded]] in ''X'' and that ''X'' is [[continuously embedded]] in ''X''<sub>1</sub>.  For <math>1\leq p, q\leq\infty</math>, let

:<math>W = \{ u \in L^p ([0, T]; X_0) \mid \dot{u} \in L^q ([0, T]; X_1) \}.</math>

(i) If <math>p<\infty</math> then the embedding of {{mvar|W}} into <math>L^p([0,T];X)</math> is compact.

(ii) If <math>p=\infty</math> and <math>q>1</math> then the embedding of {{mvar|W}} into <math>C([0,T];X)</math> is compact.
